# Coreframe Relay

> Relay sits in front of your webhook endpoint — including n8n's Production Webhook URL — counts every webhook the moment it lands, and re-sends the ones that fail.

Relay is a webhook reliability buffer, not a workflow platform: point a route
at your existing endpoint and Relay queues every request durably, retries
failed forwards with backoff, and holds anything that never succeeds in a
dead letter queue instead of letting it vanish. Delivery is at-least-once,
not exactly-once, and there is no uptime SLA, status page, or service-credit
scheme today — the Service is offered on a reasonable-endeavours basis by a
very small team (Terms §3). Relay is n8n-first today: the n8n Reliability
tier is $19/mo flat, no metering, checkout currently in Stripe test mode (a
real card is declined). There are no paying customers yet, so this site
carries no logos, testimonials, or invented numbers — a fabricated proof
point is worse than an empty section.

## Product

- [Coreframe Relay](https://relay.coreframe-labs.dev/): Webhook receipt, retry-with-backoff, and a dead letter queue in front of your existing endpoint. Buffer phase only — no metrics, customer logos, or testimonials, because there are no customers yet.
- [Pricing](https://relay.coreframe-labs.dev/pricing): n8n Reliability — $19/month flat, no metering, no usage caps, no trial clock. Checkout is a live Stripe Payment Link currently running in Stripe test mode.

## Docs

- [Documentation index](https://relay.coreframe-labs.dev/docs): Setup guides for wiring Relay in front of the thing that actually sends or receives your webhooks.
- [Quickstart — any webhook sender](https://relay.coreframe-labs.dev/docs/quickstart): Sign up, create a route, get the ingest URL, point any webhook sender at it, then what the delivery log shows and the limits (1 MiB payload cap, 64KB DLQ-replay cap, no SLA) before you rely on it. Markdown mirror: https://relay.coreframe-labs.dev/docs/quickstart.md
- [Using Relay in front of an n8n webhook](https://relay.coreframe-labs.dev/docs/integrations/n8n): The documented, current n8n Webhook-trigger bugs (silent stop, API-activation not registering the webhook path, the 100-second Cloudflare timeout, a Production Webhook that can return 200 with nothing registered), stated plainly against what Relay does and does not fix for each, plus step-by-step setup. Markdown mirror: https://relay.coreframe-labs.dev/docs/integrations/n8n.md

## Troubleshooting

- [n8n workflow deactivates itself: which bug you have, and the check that tells you](https://relay.coreframe-labs.dev/docs/troubleshooting/n8n-workflow-deactivates-itself): Three known causes by deployment shape: the multi-main activation bug (#27416, changed in n8n 2.17.0), a shared webhook path, or a trigger lost on takeover. Last verified against n8n 2.39.7 on 2026-09-17. Markdown mirror: https://relay.coreframe-labs.dev/docs/troubleshooting/n8n-workflow-deactivates-itself.md
